newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU's Lamers warns Bonn against too rigid EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: CDU's Lamers warns Bonn against too rigid EMU goal.

text.p: A leading figure in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) on Sunday said Bonn should not be bound to a too strict interpretation of the entry criteria for Europe's single currency, as advocated by Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
"The convergence criteria are not mathmatical (goals), but rather psychological," Karl Lamers, CDU foreign policy spokesman, told Berlin's Tagesspiegel newspaper in an interview.

Lamers said the Maastricht budget deficit criterion -- which aims for a deficit of three percent of gross domestic product -- initially had to be interpreted precisely in order for the necessary economic reforms to be pushed through.
"Structural reforms are decisive for the durability of stability policies and not, as some want the impression to be, the exact decimal point fulfilment of the three percent criterion," he said.
Waigel, under pressure from his Christian Social Union (CSU) to stick to a strict interpretation of Maastricht criteria, on Saturday reaffirmed his commitment to the three percent deficit target.

"We won't talk about decimal points. There is only one figure in the treaty, that is the (number) three," he told journalists at a meeting of the junior wing of the CSU, the Bavarian sister party to Kohl's CDU.

But slow economic growth and soaring unemployment -- which rose 56,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.358 million in May -- have meant Germany is struggling to fill gaping budget holes and qualify for membership of a single European currency.
Lamers said a balance had to be struck between sticking to the target of three percent and not being too rigid.

"On the one hand one must say, yes, 3.0 is our goal -- giving that up would be fatal. But on the other hand, believing one could always reach that precisely is a very mathematical conception of policy," he said.
